ai.title: Base2 prompt includes current date
ai.summary: Base2 system prompt injects current date via `formatCurrentDate(new Date())`. Uses `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with `en-US` locale, long month, numeric year/day. Affects `agents/base2/base2.ts`.

eli5.text: The assistant now mentions today's date at the start of its instructions, so you may notice references to the current date (for example, May 21, 2026) when interacting with the base system prompt. This date is generated and injected automatically each time the assistant is used, rather than being written in once and left unchanged.

ai.title: Hide empty subagent spawn errors
ai.summary: cli/src/utils/sdk-event-handlers.ts refactors spawn agent result handling to hide empty subagent spawn errors. updateSpawnAgentBlock returns null for error results with zero child blocks, filtering them out of the content tree. Scope limited to CLI SDK event handlers. Error status changed to 'complete' when non-empty blocks remain.

eli5.text: If you run a CLI command that tells the assistant to spawn a sub-agent and that sub-agent finishes without producing any output, you'll no longer see an empty or confusing error block appear in the response. The only thing you'd notice is that those silent failures are simply left out of what gets displayed. If the sub-agent did manage to produce some output before failing, that result still shows up as usual, just marked as complete instead of failed.

ai.title: Spur integration reduces VPN false positives
ai.summary: Added Spur Context API checks to free-mode IP privacy logic to corroborate IPinfo signals and reduce false positives. Schema updated with `spur_ip_privacy_signals`, `spur_status`, `privacy_decision`, and `privacy_provider_decision` columns in `free_mode_country_access_cache`. New `SPUR_TOKEN` env var required; clean Spur results restore full access in allowlisted countries, while failures fall back to limited access. Covers `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts`, `packages/internal/src/db/schema.ts`, and docs.

eli5.text: Free-tier users in supported countries who were incorrectly blocked by a VPN flag will now get full access when a second check confirms their IP address is safe. If that second check can't decide, they fall back to limited access instead of being fully locked out. The change also records the reasoning behind each access decision so the waiting-room screen can explain why you see the reduced model set without re-checking your location.

ai.title: CLI ad click tracking
ai.summary: Added ad click tracking to CLI surfaces (chat, waiting room) via new `useGravityAd` hook method `recordClick`. This sends a POST to `/api/v1/ads/click` with `impUrl` and `surface`, triggering PostHog event `ads.clicked` and DB update. Scope covers `cli/src/chat.tsx`, `cli/src/components/choice-ad-banner.tsx`, `cli/src/hooks/use-gravity-ad.ts`, and new web API route `web/src/app/api/v1/ads/click/_post.ts`. Clicks are recorded before opening the URL, with auth token required and silent failure handling.

eli5.text: When you click on a sponsored ad inside the command-line assistant (either in the main chat or the waiting room splash), the app now records that click before opening the link, letting the team measure which ads get clicked and how often. Your login token is sent along silently, and if anything goes wrong the click still opens normally with no error shown to you. The change is live today for free users and subscribers who haven't paid for an ad-free plan.

ai.title: Add chat completion trace fetcher
ai.summary: New script fetch-recent-chat-completion-traces.ts reconstructs chat completion traces from BigQuery. It queries recent sessions, applies message deltas, and writes JSON files with an index. Supports --prod, --limit, --lookback-hours, and --trace-session-id flags. Redacts secrets in previews and handles incomplete sessions.

eli5.text: A new internal tool now gathers recent chat conversations from the company's data warehouse and saves them as readable JSON files you can inspect locally, with secrets like API keys and tokens automatically hidden in previews. Engineers can ask it to pull the last few sessions from the past 24 hours, or fetch one specific session by its ID, and it pieces together full conversations from partial message updates stored across multiple records. The script lands at.context/recent-chat-completion-traces by default and writes a matching index file, and it already works today when run by an engineer with the right BigQuery access.

ai.title: Allow zero-credit API calls without balance check
ai.summary: checkCreditsAndCharge in web/src/app/api/v1/_helpers.ts returns early when creditsToCharge <= 0. This bypasses balance validation for free endpoints like web-search. Scope limited to API v1 helpers and web-search handler. Prevents 402 errors on zero-cost calls.

eli5.text: When you use a free service (like web search), the system now lets you go ahead and use it without checking whether you have any paid credits on file. Before this change, even free requests were being blocked with a 'payment needed' error because the system was still checking your balance. This only applies to specific internal helpers that handle API calls, so services like web search will now work as expected for users without requiring a balance check.

ai.title: Replace Linkup web search with Serper
ai.summary: Web search now uses Serper API instead of Linkup. Researcher agent gained `run_terminal_command` to fetch source pages directly. `LINKUP_API_KEY` replaced by `SERPER_API_KEY` in env schema and examples. Response format changed from `sourcedAnswer` to raw JSON SERP fields.

eli5.text: The web-search tool now pulls results from Serber instead of Linkup, so when an agent searches the web it gets Google-style search results (titles, links, snippets, answer boxes, related questions) rather than the old Linkup format. To set up the search, you now provide a Serber API key instead of a Linkup key, and the example config file and schema have been updated to match. The research agent can also open those result pages directly using a terminal command, which lets it read full articles, not just the short snippets the search returns.

ai.title: Add readurl tool for web research
ai.summary: New read_url tool added to agent toolset, enabling direct URL fetching and text extraction. Replaces curl usage in researcher-web agent, now using read_url alongside web_search. Covers SDK, agent runtime, common tools, and type definitions. Input schema validates http/https URLs with optional max_chars (default 20000, max 50000).

eli5.text: When the research assistant tries to look up information online, it can now grab the full text of a webpage directly instead of using a separate command-line tool to fetch it. This makes web research faster and smoother for anyone who asks the assistant to gather information from specific web pages. You would notice this if you watched the assistant working because it would simply read webpage contents without first running a manual fetching step.

ai.title: Add readurl tool to base2 agent and CLI registry
ai.summary: The `read_url` tool is now available to the `base2` agent and registered in the CLI tool component registry. This change introduces a new capability for the agent to fetch and process content from URLs, accompanied by a dedicated UI component (`ReadURLComponent`) for displaying the tool's execution. The update spans `agents/base2/base2.ts`, `cli/src/components/tools/read-url.tsx`, and `cli/src/components/tools/registry.ts`. The new tool is unconditionally enabled for the agent, unlike some other tools which are gated by flags like `isFree` or `noAskUser`.

eli5.text: When you talk with the agent named base2, it can now fetch and show you the contents of a web page just by giving it a link, instead of being unable to reach outside sources. If you watched the agent working, you would see it list the URL it grabbed in its usual compact display card, the same style it uses for reading local files. This ability is turned on for everyone using base2 right away, with no special setting or extra key needed.

ai.title: Bump CLI release to 1.0.678
ai.summary: Version field in cli/release/package.json incremented from 1.0.677 to 1.0.678 as part of the scheduled release-bump commit for the 2026-05-21 build. This is accompanied by the following user-visible changes since 1.0.677: read_files now accepts absolute paths within the project root and maps normalized loadedFiles to fix path mismatches (common/src/tools/params/tool/read-files.ts, packages/agent-runtime/src/get-file-reading-updates.ts); CLI API client in cli/src/utils/codebuff-api.ts resolves proxy URLs from HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY env vars (pass proxy: null to disable); free-mode IP privacy checks consult a new Spur Context API alongside IPinfo in common/src/util/freebuff-privacy.ts and packages/internal/src/db/schema.ts to reduce VPN false positives (SPUR_TOKEN required); and the /live and web surfaces removed redundant explanatory subtitles/country codes and clarified limited-mode reason text in the waiting room.
ai.evidence: cli/release/package.json hunks version field from "1.0.677" to "1.0.678" in commit c75442472026-05-21T20:54:22Z (release-bump, only file cli/release/package.json modified).

eli5.text: This release adds a new web-reading tool called read_url that lets you browse and analyze webpage content directly, plus it swaps out the old web search engine for a new one (Serper) for better results. VPN and proxy users are now blocked from accessing Freebuff, with clear messages telling you why, while everyone else gets smoother error handling when the system is busy. The upgrade also quietly improves things behind the scenes: your chat sessions now send better analytics so you get the right access tier, ad clicks are tracked in the terminal, and file reading works with absolute paths so you can point to any file in your project. Upgrading gives you more reliable web research, clearer error messages when things go wrong, and a cleaner experience whether you're in the waiting room or chatting with an agent.

ai.title: Freebuff 0.0.95 release with onboarding, search, and tool updates
ai.summary: This release bumps the Freebuff version to 0.0.95, shipping onboarding auth-code handling, web search migration to Serper, the new read_url tool, Spur IP privacy checks, CLI ad click tracking, chat completion trace fetches, and current-date injection for base2. The version field in cli/release/package.json increments from 0.0.94 to 0.0.95 per the release-bump commit. Several changes touch user-visible surfaces: the onboarding flow renders a static expired-link card when CLI auth codes are missing, base2 now receives the current date in its system prompt, and the CLI can record ad clicks via a new useGravityAd hook. API-level updates include zero-credit calls bypassing balance checks and replacement of Linkup API keys with SERPER_API_KEY in env schemas and examples.
ai.evidence: The diff shows a single line change in freebuff/cli/release/package.json bumping the version field from 0.0.94 to 0.0.95, a standard release-bump commit.

ai.title: Web search tool renderer for CLI
ai.summary: Added `WebSearchComponent` to render `web_search` tool calls in the CLI. Registered in `cli/src/components/tools/registry.ts`. Displays search query via `SimpleToolCallItem`.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to search the web from the chat command line, the search request now shows up as a small labeled card that prints the exact question you asked, instead of showing up as raw technical input. The terminal interface now has a dedicated display component mapped to the web search action, so each search is presented in a readable, consistent format. This behavior is live today for anyone running the assistant from the command line and triggering a web search tool call.
